text:
anya: Nightly eval alert — Llama-3-small-quant: chat-promptset-chat-ops failing at +18% error rate vs baseline on last nightly.

mike: Upped to look — reproduced locally when running with concurrent batches. Seems to happen only when quantized model + shared prefix cache is enabled. :thinking:

lucas: I instrumented the KV layer. Here's the failing log snippet:
```
KVLookup: key_shorthash=0x4f2a, tenant=redwood, slot=123
KVLookup: found slot -> owner=tenant_b (mismatch)
Generation: stray context tokens in output -> bad generation
```
This matches a shorthash aliasing scenario.

anya: Interesting. Any recent changes that could affect shorthash distribution or cache salt?

lucas: PR #4124 tweaked `prefix_cache_salt` default to improve hit rate for small prefixes. But I think the bigger effect is the new narrow-batching scheduler in runtime that interleaves prefixes across requests more often.

mike: Repro steps I used:
```
export BATCH_SIZE=32
export ENABLE_PREFIX_KV=1
./runtime --model=llama-3-small-quant --seed=42 --concurrent=8 --run-eval chat-ops
```
With seed 42 I get deterministic bad outputs most runs when both quant and prefix-kv are enabled.

ci-bot: nightly-run 1955554000: regression detected on dataset `chat-promptset-chat-ops` (failure_count increased by 18%). Tags: regression, cache-collision.

eva: Short-term mitigation: turn off cross-tenant prefix aliasing and set `prefix_cache_salt` per-tenant. Long-term: add salt + eviction tie-breaker and deterministic assignment for shorthash collisions.

anya: Can we also add a unit/regression test in nightly that simulates interleaved narrow-batches and asserts generation determinism?

lucas: Yes. Plan: (1) add per-tenant salt, (2) add deterministic eviction (LRU tie-breaker using request-id), (3) add unit test harness that seeds scheduler and ensures stable generations for quantized models. I'll open PR and tag eng-ml + eng-runtime. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

mike: I'll help with the test harness and add a Golden-output check for chat-ops.

anya: Awesome. For tracking: creating a follow-up issue and tagging for roll-forward. :+1:
